_note: Build-time tokens. Replace all of these BEFORE running the MJML compile (see docs/mail-templates.md). Runtime %field% placeholders are NOT listed here and must never be replaced — submit.php fills those on every send.

_colour_rules.principle: Structure is neutral, accent is branded. Small elements (a 3px rule, link text) can take a client's colour at full strength because their contrast demands are low. Large text-bearing fills cannot.
_colour_rules.hue_follows_value_does_not: BRAND_DARK may take the client's HUE but never their VALUE. Clamp lightness to 12-18% and saturation to 10-25%, so contrast against BRAND_DARK_MUTED is guaranteed by construction rather than checked per client.
_colour_rules.accent_floor: BRAND_ACCENT must clear 4.5:1 against BRAND_SURFACE. It colours link text as well as the flag, so a pale brand colour is a legibility failure, not just a weak-looking rule.
_colour_rules.footer_text_floor: BRAND_DARK_MUTED must clear 4.5:1 against BRAND_DARK. Recheck whenever BRAND_DARK changes.
_colour_rules.count_discipline: BRAND_ACCENT appears exactly twice (flag, clickable values). BRAND_DARK appears exactly twice and always as the same value (card border, footer band). Adding a third occurrence of either dilutes both.

_kicker_note: %kicker% is the one placeholder submit.php doesn't build straight from POST data — build_kicker() joins the form-type field (a plain hidden <input name="form_type"> on the contact form, index.html/pt/index.html), the date, and the language code with a middle dot, dropping whichever parts don't apply (form-type and language are both omitted for the reply build — form-type's value is fixed in the OWNER's language, so it can't appear in a visitor-facing email; language is redundant to whoever just submitted the form in it). Used identically by all three templates via contact/_partials/_kicker.mjml.

CLIENT_NAME.note: Wordmark text, footer name, credit line, notification preview text.

CLIENT_URL.note: Site root, not a page — same value regardless of which language template sends the email. See the comment in _header.mjml for why.

CLIENT_LOGO_URL.note: Only once the client has a logo PNG. Until then _header.mjml ships a text wordmark that needs no image asset — see the swap comment at the top of that file. Must be publicly reachable, never under starter/app/templates/ (.htaccess-locked).

CLIENT_PHONE.note: Display form, with spaces. CLIENT_PHONE_RAW is derived from this, not asked separately.

CLIENT_PHONE_RAW.note: DO NOT ASK THE CLIENT FOR THIS. Derive it at build time from CLIENT_PHONE by stripping everything except digits and a leading +. Asking for the same number twice in two formats is a papercut in the instantiation flow, and a hand-typed second copy is a chance to get it wrong.

CLIENT_INSTAGRAM.note: Delete the whole <a> if the client has no account — an empty href is worse than no link.

BRAND_FONT.note: Email-safe stacks only. No web fonts — most mail clients strip external font loading entirely.

BRAND_FONT_HEADING.note: Only affects the heading. Set to "Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif" for editorial or creative clients.

BRAND_ACCENT.note: THE per-client colour: the accent flag and clickable values. Everything structural (border, footer band) stays neutral across all clients — see BRAND_DARK. Must clear 4.5:1 against BRAND_SURFACE, because this token also colours link text, not just the 3px rule.

BRAND_MUTED.note: All four field labels, kicker, credit.

BRAND_FRAME.note: Set to #ffffff for a flat, frameless look — the card border still defines the card.

BRAND_DARK.note: Card border AND footer band — must be the same value. That identity is the design. NOT the raw brand colour: this fill carries light text, so an arbitrary brand hue fails contrast. If you want it to feel client-specific, derive it — take the brand's hue, clamp lightness to 12-18% and saturation to 10-25% (navy brand -> #1e2530, terracotta -> #2e211b). Same hue as the client, contrast guaranteed by construction. Leave at #2b2926 when the client has no colour scheme.

BRAND_DARK_MUTED.note: Footer copy. Must clear 4.5:1 against BRAND_DARK.

BRAND_RADIUS.note: Card corners. 0px for a hard-edged corporate feel. Outlook squares these regardless.

BRAND_RADIUS_INNER.note: Always BRAND_RADIUS minus 1px. footer-band's own bottom corners sit just inside card-body's 1px border, so they read as one continuous curve rather than two concentric ones — see 'Mail template gotchas' in docs/mail-templates.md for why there's no single wrapper carrying the border across both.
